_why: THE COST-SLOPE SWEEP, BATCH 2 - THE BISECTION UP (pre-registered in batch 1's schedule: 'above the GDP target band -> C 1.9'). Batch 1, canon-c16-in12 (session 20260914_143137), read 1.04 / 0.98 / 0.99 / 1.04 / 1.07 / 1.12 / 1.27 / 1.59x vanilla's eighteen-run median at 1850..1920 in its first run - on vanilla's path to 1890, then the explosive regime (A 1.9 flat's shape: 1.27-1.41x at 1900, 1.8x at 1936) - and the run-level stop rule (user-ruled 2026-09-14: a 2+1 run above x1.3 of vanilla's 1936 GDP is the config's last) ends that config at n=1 if the endpoint confirms it. So the slope moves up: this book is canon-je24-a22-in12 with building_cost = anchor x 1.9^era (600 / 1,140 / 2,166 / 4,115 and 800 / 1,520 / 2,888 / 5,487) - between C 1.6 (the world takes off after 1890) and C 2.2 (0.65x, the frontier too scarce, F113) - everything else identical (A 2.2 / B 1.5, era-0 inputs x1.2 with the ladder anchored on it, ai_value 1,000x3^era, divisor 0.000125, the 10.75 defines, the 24-month bar, the era-rule canon's structure). The response is a regime change, not a line: at C 1.6 the frontier's capital is cheap enough that the loop (cheap capacity -> GDP -> pools -> more capacity) runs away after 1890; at C 2.2 the frontier never fills. NEXT (one more bisection): above the band -> C 2.05; below -> C 1.75; then the x1.3 lift at the found C.
